title: Operating Mode
description:
Declarative, data-driven contract for a swarm-manager operating mode — a reusable, inspectable, testable methodology loop for agentic software engineering. One generic engine interprets this data; there is NO vocabulary bespoke to a named mode. A mode lives in `scenarios/swarm-manager/modes/<id>/` as `mode.json` (this contract, kind `operating-mode`) and `example-runs/` (simulation fixtures, kind `operating-mode-example-run`). Phase prompts live as prompt-manager skills reached through `prompt.catalog_prefix` + phase prompt suffix. One schema covers both document kinds, discriminated by the top-level `kind` field.

DOCTRINE (canonical: scenarios/swarm-manager/docs/concepts/EXECUTION-MODES.md):

1. DATA IS THE SSOT. A methodology loop is a specification — a phase graph, checkpoints, what each phase reads and emits, how branches are chosen. It belongs in data one interpreter reads, not smeared across Go source. Adding or changing a mode is a data edit, not a code change.

2. GENERIC VOCABULARY. Branching is a generic field-predicate guard model (field-path, operator, value, with all/any/not composition) that can express any phase DAG — a clean pass, a replan loop, a continue-draining branch, a blocked stop, a non-accepting review reloop. There is no closed, mode-specific set of branch kinds; a branch is just a predicate over declared output.

3. DECLARED OUTPUT STEERS ROBUSTNESS. Each phase declares what a round is supposed to emit (field name/type/required/enum/bounds). That single artifact both validates a round's result and steers the resolution ladder (L0 true-final-message detection → L1 deterministic extraction → L2 AI-classifier fallback → L3 contract validation) when model output is imperfect. The mode declares WHAT good output is; the engine does HOW to obtain it.

4. EXAMPLE-RUNS ARE TESTS. A mode is simulated and asserted before it is trusted: example-run documents seed phase outputs and assert the expected phase path through the REAL guards. They are also the data behind the UI's simulation presets.

What JSON Schema cannot express is enforced by the engine's semantic validator (mirroring knowledge-observatory's validateContent): start_phase and every transition target resolve to a declared phase; auto_start_after references a declared phase; guard field-paths resolve against the source phase's declared output; profile keys are scenario-owned; example-run steps and expected_path reference declared phases; phase reads resolve against the mode's composed provider set (generic base ∪ target adapter — read-side validation, symmetric with the emit-side checks); and per-target semantics (phase graph present for every phase mode; lock exclusive and backlog-sync apply mode set on initiative-target modes).

Identifier.description: Kebab-case identifier, stable once published (other files, guards, and example-runs reference it).

PhaseId.description: Phase node id within a mode's graph. Kebab or snake case (existing phases use both, e.g. `execute`, `prepare_plan`, `classify_progress`).

ProfileKey.description: AgentManager profile key. Must be scenario-owned (`swarm-manager/…`); the engine rejects non-scenario-owned keys. Profile JSON remains the source of profile defaults — the mode only references which key applies.

ReadName.description: A prompt-facing input alias, e.g. `PRIOR_ROUNDS_JSON`, `MEMBER_ITEMS_JSON`, `PLAN_PATH`. Every alias resolves through the mode's input_contract to a logical InputSpec and one explicit source binding.

InputId.description: Stable dotted logical input identity, independent of acquisition provider (for example `execution.operator_note` or `plan.context`).

InputContract.description: Mode-level input SSOT. Specs own logical value semantics, sources own acquisition policy, and aliases bind prompt variables to logical inputs. The semantic compiler rejects missing/competing sources, unavailable capabilities, target mismatches, cycles, conflicting retention, and unused aliases.

FieldPath.description: Dotted path into a round's structured output envelope (e.g. `replan_needed`, `progress.decision`, `handoff.frontier`). Guards and declared-output field names use this shape.

ModeDocument.description: A single operating mode expressed as data. Identity + decision metadata, target (unit of work), run strategy, the phase graph, and per-concern policy blocks. Every mode runs mode rounds through a required `phase_graph`.

schema_version.description: Optional semantic version of this mode document, independent of the schema $id.

id.description: Stable mode id and the folder name under `modes/`. `item-level` is reserved (the member-item workflow strategy sentinel, not a mode).

label.description: Human-facing mode name shown in the picker and detail page.

description.description: One-paragraph description of the methodology and when to use it.

best_for.description: Work shapes this mode is the right pick for. Decision support in the picker; ≥1 required.

not_for.description: Work shapes this mode handles poorly; ≥1 required.

tradeoffs.description: Structural tradeoffs an operator accepts by choosing this mode; ≥1 required.

when_in_doubt_pick_instead.description: Mode id an operator should pick if unsure between this one and another. Omit (or empty) when this mode is itself the safe default. The engine verifies it references a registered mode and is not self.

allOf.description: Every mode declares one input contract, runs a phase graph, routes prompts through a catalog prefix, and owns an artifact root.

then.description: Initiative-target phase modes additionally reconcile the backlog under a declared apply mode and hold the initiative lock exclusively.

TargetPolicy.description: The mode's declared unit of work — what one run of the loop operates on. Each kind has a target adapter supplying the target-specific reads, artifact scope, and lock identity; initiative is one adapter among several, not the base case.

kind.description: backlog-item = a single swarm-manager backlog item (vocabulary is pinned; its runtime adapter arrives in a later phase). initiative = a swarm-manager initiative and its member items. plan-execution = a canonical, provider-neutral plan execution (the resolved instance carries plan id + execution id). scenario = a plain scenario repository workspace (a scenario directory) identified by scenario name, with no owning item/initiative/plan (used by spec-sync). NOTE: the domain plan_ref FIELD on items/initiatives is an associated Plan Manager reference, never a target kind; the pre-cutover unmanaged plan-ref target kind is removed.

else.description: The bound-plan contract (plan_ref) is initiative-adapter configuration; plan targets ARE plans and must not declare it.

RunStrategyPolicy.description: How rounds are dispatched and gated.

kind.description: single_phase_run = one phase at a time with no cross-round handoff requirement. sequential_handoff = each non-start phase requires durable handoff/progress context from the prior completed round. operator_gated_loop = the operator advances the loop between rounds.

PhaseGraph.description: The phase state-machine: nodes (phases), the start node, terminal nodes, and per-phase guarded transitions. The engine derives the static adjacency (allowed next phases) from the union of every transition's `to`.

start_phase.description: The first phase; must be one of `phases`.

terminal.description: Phases that end the loop. Each must be one of `phases`.

phases.description: The phase nodes, in a natural reading order. Each declares its kind, prompt, declared output, transitions, and policy.

PhaseDefinition.description: One node in the phase graph — a distinct step of the loop. A regular phase declares what it reads (the `reads` input contract), what it emits (declared_output + output_artifacts), and where it routes (transitions). A DELEGATED phase instead declares `executed_by: <sub-mode-id>` — the engine runs the sub-mode's loop as that phase (its rounds use the sub-mode's prompts, reads, and classified edges under the parent's run and target), and the sub-mode's terminal outcome becomes this phase's resolved output for the parent's `transitions` to route on. A delegated phase therefore declares NO reads/prompt/declared_output/artifacts of its own; exactly one composition level is allowed (a sub-mode may not itself contain delegated phases — the loader rejects nesting, self-delegation, and unknown sub-modes).

then.description: A delegated phase's execution surface (prompt, reads, emits, artifacts, profile, purposes) comes entirely from the sub-mode's phases; declaring any of it on the delegating phase is a contradiction.

else.description: A regular phase must declare its activity purpose and its reads input contract.

executed_by.description: Sub-mode id that executes this phase (phase delegation, EXECUTION-MODES.md D3). The engine runs the sub-mode's loop as this phase, one level deep: sub-rounds persist under the parent run tagged with this phase id, an onward sub-route keeps the phase in progress, and a sub-mode stop surfaces its outcome (e.g. the classified `progress` value) as this phase's result for the parent's transitions to route on. The delegating mode's target must supply the sub-mode's target context: same target kind, or an initiative-target mode with `target.plan_ref.required` delegating to a `plan-execution`-target sub-mode (the initiative's bound plan is the sub-mode's plan).

reads.description: The phase's declared input contract: the named variables its prompt template may reference, symmetric with declared_output on the emit side. Composed as generic-base provider ∪ target-adapter provider — a union, never a conditional. The engine validates at load time that every declared read is satisfiable by the mode's composed provider set, and substitutes exactly the declared reads at render time.

kind.description: Phase classification. Lane assignment, Operations Center column placement, and per-lane metric grouping key off this axis. Descriptive, not restrictive — a mode may define any phases; each declares its kind.

activity_purpose.description: Stable activity purpose token for the spawned agent run (e.g. `holistic_loop_investigate`). Used for audit/event provenance.

lock_purpose.description: Lock purpose token; defaults to `activity_purpose` when omitted.

auto_start_after.description: Single predecessor phase whose successful completion auto-starts this phase via the round-refresher hook. Length ≤ 1 (multi-predecessor is rejected to avoid race design pressure). Fires only on completed (not failed/cancelled) rounds after the initiative lock is released.

writes_repo.description: True when the phase's agent modifies the repository (execute-style phases). Drives sandbox/write posture.

requires_criteria.description: True when the phase cannot start without initiative acceptance criteria (review phases).

profile_key.description: AgentManager profile for this phase's agent run. Falls back to the mode's `profile.default_profile_key` when omitted.

output_artifacts.description: Files the phase is expected to produce under the mode's artifact root.

evidence_requirements.description: Canonical evidence facts required before this phase can complete. Missing evidence remains pending until the named producer has terminal coverage for the run and subject kind.

result_bindings.description: Bindings that persist a structured result field into a durable artifact.

transitions.description: Ordered guarded edges out of this phase. The first transition whose guard matches selects the next phase(s). Omit for a terminal phase, or use a single `{ "when": {"op":"always"}, "to": [next] }` for an unconditional edge. An empty `to` is a guarded stop (e.g. a `blocked` progress decision).

EvidenceRequirement.description: A normalized, mode-data verification predicate over the canonical evidence ledger. It intentionally names no mode-specific vocabulary.

subject_kind.description: Normalized evidence subject kind, such as plan, artifact, file, repository_change, or cli_invocation.

action.description: Normalized fact action required for the subject.

producer.description: Optional canonical evidence producer id. Omit only for requirements satisfied by any producer; an omitted producer cannot turn absence into definitive missing evidence.

min_count.description: Number of matching facts required before the gate is satisfied.

match_fields.description: Bounded metadata fields that must exactly match the evidence observation.

PhasePrompt.description: Prompt routing for the phase. `suffix` composes the catalog/skill id with the mode's `prompt.catalog_prefix`; title/trigger/purpose are catalog metadata.

template.description: Deprecated legacy field. Phase prompt bodies now live as prompt-manager skills reached through the resolved catalog/skill id.

suffix.description: Catalog/skill id suffix; the id is `<mode prompt.catalog_prefix>-<suffix>`. Defaults to the phase id when omitted.

trigger.description: One-line description of what triggers this phase's prompt.

purpose.description: One-line description of the phase's purpose.

DeclaredOutput.description: The per-phase contract for what a round is supposed to emit — the single artifact that validates a round's result AND steers the resolution ladder. Unifies the older scattered output-contract flags (requires_progress/verdict/handoff/backlog_sync) into one declared field set.

envelope_key.description: Top-level JSON key the structured result is nested under in agent output. Defaults to `operating_mode_result`.

requires_structured_result.description: Whether a structured result envelope is required at all. Initiative-scoped phases require it.

fields.description: The declared fields of the structured result. Guards reference these by field-path.

OutputField.description: One declared output field: name/type/required/enum/bounds, with optional nested fields for object types. This is the generic field vocabulary the resolution ladder extracts and validates against.

name.description: Field name (or dotted path for a nested leaf, e.g. `progress.decision`). Guards reference this exact path.

required.description: Whether L3 validation fails when the field is absent.

enum.description: Closed set of permitted values (e.g. progress.decision ∈ continue/blocked/replan/complete).

minimum.description: Inclusive lower bound for integer/number fields.

maximum.description: Inclusive upper bound for integer/number fields.

description.description: What the field means; also steers the L2 classifier.

fields.description: Nested fields for an object-typed field. An alternative to dotted-path leaf declarations for structured sub-objects.

ResolutionPolicy.description: Per-phase resolution-ladder tuning. Data declares WHAT; the engine does HOW.

detect_true_final_message.description: L0: scan the last N agent messages for the declared output shape to find the true final message (agents sometimes append subagent tails after a 'final' message). Set false to opt out and treat the last message as final.

scan_last_n_messages.description: How many trailing agent messages L0 scans when detecting the true final message.

allow_classifier.description: L2: allow the AI-classifier fallback (steered by this declared output) when deterministic extraction (L1) cannot cleanly extract. When false, an L1 miss is an honest abstain with no model call.

Transition.description: One edge out of a phase: a guarded edge (`when`/`to`), or a classified edge (`classify`/`routes`) that derives the routing field from the completed round's output at the edge (classification-on-transition). A phase may declare at most one classified edge.

oneOf.description: A guarded edge. When `when` matches the completed round's output, the loop routes to `to`.

to.description: Target phase(s). Usually one; may be several to offer the operator a choice. Empty = a guarded stop (no onward phase).

oneOf.description: A classified edge. The engine derives `classify.field` from the completed round's output (emitted field short-circuits; deterministic extraction from `<from>.<field>` is L1; the schema-steered classifier is L2; an underivable field abstains and the round parks in needs_attention) and routes on it via `routes` — expanded by the loader into ordinary eq-guards in declared enum order.

additionalProperties.description: Target phase(s) for this routing value. Empty = a guarded stop (no onward phase).

routes.description: Map from each declared enum value to its target phase(s). Every `classify.enum` value must appear exactly once; keys outside the enum are rejected.

ClassificationContract.description: A transition-owned classification contract: how to derive the routing field from the just-completed round's output when it was not directly emitted. The declaration is data — the engine owns the ladder mechanics. An emitted field always wins (classification is a fallback, not a toll); a routing decision is never fabricated.

field.description: Dotted path of the routing field to derive (e.g. `progress.decision`). The expanded route guards compare this field. Must not be declared REQUIRED in the phase's declared_output (a required field is always emitted, permanently short-circuiting the classification — use plain guarded transitions instead); declaring it optional is allowed.

enum.description: Closed set of permitted routing values. The L2 classifier is hard-constrained to this set and abstains rather than guessing outside it.

from.description: Declared output field of the phase to derive from (e.g. `handoff`). L1 reads the value inline at `<from>.<field>`; L2 classifies the JSON of this field's value. Omitted = the whole structured result envelope.

description.description: What the routing decision means; steers the L2 classifier.

Guard.description: A generic field-predicate over a round's structured output. Leaf forms compare a field-path to a value; `all`/`any`/`not` compose leaves into any boolean expression, so the guard vocabulary can express any phase DAG with no mode-specific branch kinds.

oneOf.description: Unconditional guard — always matches (the default/fallback edge).
Presence guard — matches on whether a field is present (and non-null).
Comparison guard — compares a field's value. `eq`/`ne` for any JSON scalar; `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte` for numbers.

value.description: Scalar compared against the field's value.

oneOf.description: Membership guard — matches when the field's value is in the set.
Conjunction — matches when every sub-guard matches.
Disjunction — matches when at least one sub-guard matches.
Negation — matches when the sub-guard does not match.

ArtifactDefinition.description: A file the phase produces or a binding writes.

path.description: Path relative to the mode's artifact root (e.g. `modes/holistic-loop/findings.md`).

required.description: Whether the phase output contract requires this artifact.

ResultBinding.description: Persists a structured-result field into a durable artifact.

kind.description: The binding kind. `progress_artifact` writes the round's progress state to a JSON artifact.

PhaseMetrics.description: Per-phase flags the engine aggregates into the mode's metrics policy.

counts_replan_sample.description: This phase's rounds count toward the replan-rate sample.

counts_acceptance_sample.description: This phase's rounds count toward the acceptance-rate sample.

catalog_prefix.description: Prefix for every phase's catalog/skill id; the id is `<catalog_prefix>-<phase prompt.suffix>` (e.g. `swarm-manager-holistic-loop`).

round_root.description: Per-round artifact directory. Defaults to `<root>/rounds` when omitted.

PlanRefPolicy.description: Initiative-adapter configuration (nested under `target`): the contract for a canonical plan-manager reference bound to the initiative. When required, the start phase may emit it and subsequent phases consume it through the PLAN_CONTEXT_JSON read. This is the domain plan_ref FIELD (an associated Plan Manager reference), distinct from the plan-execution target kind where a plan execution itself is the unit of work.

required.description: True when this mode requires an initiative plan_ref before non-start phases run.

role.description: The semantic role of the referenced plan.

ProfilePolicy.description: Mode-level profile defaults. Per-phase overrides live on each phase's `profile_key`; the engine derives the phase→profile map.

default_profile_key.description: Fallback profile for phases that don't declare one.

BacklogSyncPolicy.description: How the mode reads and reconciles the initiative backlog.

capabilities.description: What the mode may do to the backlog. Initiative modes get the full set.

requires_run_id.description: Reconcile/complete actions require a run id.

requires_membership.description: Backlog-sync targets must be initiative members.

event_source.description: Event-source tag for emitted backlog-sync events. Defaults to the mode id.

apply_mode.description: How reconcile proposals are committed. Only `operator-gated` is implemented; the auto-apply variants fail loudly at the apply seam. Required on initiative-scoped modes.

MetricsPolicy.description: Mode-level metrics configuration. Sample-phase lists are derived from per-phase `metrics` flags; declare `accepted_verdicts` here.

event_source.description: Event-source tag for emitted metrics events. Defaults to the mode id.

accepted_verdicts.description: Verdict strings that count as acceptance (e.g. `accept`, `accepted`). Case-insensitive at match time.

initiative_exclusive.description: True when only one mode round may run against the initiative at a time (all initiative-scoped modes).

workspace_tab_id.description: Which initiative workspace tab this mode's controls render under (e.g. `operating-mode`, `info`).

ExampleRunDocument.description: A mode-owned simulation fixture. It seeds each step's phase output and asserts the phase path the REAL generic guard evaluator produces. Example-runs are how a mode is tested before use and are the data behind the UI's simulation presets. They never spawn agents, acquire locks, or persist state.

id.description: Preset id; the example-run's stable handle (e.g. `replan-loop`, `clean-pass`).

mode.description: The mode this example-run exercises. The engine verifies it matches the owning folder.

label.description: Human-facing preset name shown in the Flow tab's data-source control.

branch.description: One-line summary of the guarded branch this preset exercises (e.g. `execute → investigate (replan_needed)`). Operator-facing.

scenario.description: Prose narrative of the work shape this preset represents. Operator-facing; explains why the branch is taken.

initiative.description: The ephemeral sandbox initiative this preset seeds — the items, acceptance criteria, and framing the simulated rounds run against. Omit to use generic defaults.

steps.description: Ordered seeded rounds. Each step names the phase it runs and the structured output to feed the guards. The walk starts at the mode's start_phase; step N's seeded output selects the transition into step N+1's phase. Provide one step per non-terminal phase visit in order; the terminal phase takes no step.

expected_path.description: The exact ordered phase path the guards must produce for this fixture. The simulation asserts the walked path equals this.

ExampleRunInitiative.description: The seeded sandbox initiative an example-run's simulated rounds run against. Purely illustrative fixture data; never persisted.

title.description: Initiative title shown in the simulation header.

description.description: Short framing of the initiative's work.

items.description: Seeded backlog items in scope, shown in each step's inputs.

criteria.description: Acceptance criteria the review phase evaluates against.

ExampleRunItem.description: One seeded backlog item in an example-run's sandbox initiative.

ExampleRunStep.description: One seeded round in an example-run.

phase.description: The phase this step runs. Must be a declared phase of the mode.

output.description: Seeded structured output for this round (the contents of the declared_output envelope), fed to the source phase's transition guards. Omit for phases with only an unconditional edge.

note.description: Optional human note explaining what this step demonstrates.
